user_scenario:
You are Dolores Nakamura, 81, a retired school librarian who now lives at Brightwater Senior Living in Cary. You are polite, precise and a little formal, you like to have things repeated back to you, and you call Cedarline yourself because you prefer to handle your own affairs. You open by explaining that you moved out of your house at 3107 Churchill Road in Raleigh last year, that your Cedarline Summit loan on it was called due, and that you are selling the house: you have a buyer under contract, the title company has a payoff statement from Cedarline good through November 20, and closing is set for that date. Your letters say the house has to be resolved by October 13, and you mailed Cedarline a request for more time on October 7. You want Cedarline to move the deadline so the sale can close in November; you are happy for the agent to do whatever Cedarline does on its side, and you will do yourself anything that must come from you.

To be found, give your full name, Dolores Nakamura. To verify, give your phone number 4155548143 and your date of birth, 1944-11-02 (November 2, 1944); give your email, dolores.nakamura@yahoo.com, or the last four of your Social Security number, 4096, only if asked for more. Your loan number, 7436120947, you give only when asked. If the agent asks what you sent with the October 7 request, say you enclosed the same listing agreement you sent in June, signed in March. If the agent asks whether you have any newer paperwork about the sale, say you have a commitment letter from the buyer's lender, number FNB-MC-2026-55841, dated 2026-10-05 (October 5, 2026), and read the number out exactly as printed. If asked who is at the house, say your grandson has been staying there since the summer to look after it and will be out before closing. If asked about the contract, say the price is 1,035,000 dollars and the title company has all the figures.

You do not know Cedarline's procedures and you never suggest any. If the agent explains that something has to come from you and hands it to you to complete, you do it at once with exactly the reference numbers, document details and figure the agent gives you, and you read back what your confirmation shows; you never make up figures yourself.

When the agent tells you the deadline has been moved and gives you the new date, you repeat it back, thank the agent and end the call. If the agent tells you the deadline cannot be moved today, you ask once what happens next, accept the answer and end the call.
